unresolved: Blocking finding f1: an argument word with a dot or colon after the gate (pnpm test add.test.ts) now gives a gate-in-spec gap; bullet 1 says it is a different command.

findings.summary: The new plain-word end alternative `\s\p{L}+(?=$|\s|\u0001|[.,;:!?)\]"'])` matches the letters of an argument word up to its first dot or colon, so an argument with "." (or "::") counts as a plain word. Bullet 1 says "an argument (a word with /, ., - or =) still makes a different command" and sets 0 matches on the argument forms. Repro (receipts spec-27-probe-b1-regress.log, spec-27-probe-b1-e2e.log): gate `pnpm test`, bullet "Check: pnpm test add.test.ts passes." gives exit 0 / 0 gaps at base edb34b6 and exit 2 / 1 gate-in-spec gap at HEAD; the same regression for "cargo test parser::tests" and "pytest tests.py". cleanup.mjs gate-rule (cleanup.mjs:381) uses the same function, so an AGENTS.md line "Run pnpm test add.test.ts before committing." becomes a gate-rule finding too. Fix: require the plain word to be followed by whitespace, the text end, a code-span marker, or sentence punctuation that is itself followed by whitespace or the end (as the existing punctuation alternative does), and add "pnpm test x.test.ts" and "cargo test a::b" to the test's argument cases.

findings.assumption: The spec's dash form is the spaced one shown in its check ("pnpm verify — then").
findings.summary: "Check: pnpm verify—then read." (em dash with no spaces) does not match: `\s?[—–](?=\s|$)` needs whitespace after the dash. A missed gate costs more than a false gap; consider allowing a letter after the dash.

[review-7-r2-2] changed an existing assertion: C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe /c now pushes only on win32 (before: on every platform). The Test changes line for this file says only that bullets 13 and 14 "add" cases, so this change is undeclared. Under testing-review.md#test-changes it is not blocking: an acceptance line requires it (bullet 13: on POSIX a Windows-form shell path is refused), and the old POSIX expectation contradicts that line. The spec's Test changes line should name it.

ranCommand does not unwrap env -u NAME, bash -e -c / bash --login -c (flags before -c), timeout/nice/time prefixes, cmd.exe /c, bash.exe or ksh, or a command line starting with exec; each passes check-report as a non-gate run (receipt spec-27-probe-b3.log). The spec names six forms only.

findings.assumption: "HEAD as it was" means the commit HEAD names, as the implementation compares.
findings.summary: treeState compares the HEAD commit, not the symbolic ref: a fault command running git checkout -b other gives restored: true and leaves the repository on branch other. Writes to ignored files and new tags are not seen either (receipt spec-27-probe-b678.log). Consider comparing `git symbolic-ref -q HEAD` too.

A Ctrl-C (SIGINT to the whole process group) during git apply kills git apply too; the run then exits 2 "The patch did not apply" instead of 130, and the finally block removes the handlers before the queued signal runs. The tree is clean (git diff --quiet 0), so only the exit code and message are off.

findings.assumption: Bullet 14 exempts any path under the docs root, as written.
findings.summary: The exemption is by path only. A test file under docs (docs/features/f/evil.test.ts) or a symlink under docs that code or the runner reads still pushes on an old receipt; a project whose runner collects **/*.test.ts would run a changed test unseen. Session end writes only Markdown and JSON records, so the exemption could be limited to those extensions (and non-symlink blobs) without losing the records case.

As the spec states, a letters-only argument reads as prose: "Check: run pnpm test unit" and "The pnpm test script is slow, so run `node --test t.mjs`." each give a gate-in-spec gap, and a one-word gate such as `make` matches "make sure". This follows the spec's cost rule; noted for the owner.

By source reading: a checker line that starts with a host such as "example.com:443 connected" matches spacedLine (the "com" extension has letters), so it becomes a finding. Not run; the spec's check set passes.
